message.content: {"ranking": [{"id": "patch_2e6db5d7770e", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 9010, "mechanism": "The failing trace shows o_mosi stuck at 0 when it should toggle during command framing. The original code enters the r_cmd_state == 3'h0 branch on every pre_cmd_state pulse without checking whether ll_cmd_stb is already asserted from a previous cycle. This causes the state machine to re-send the first command byte (r_data_reg[31:24]) and re-assert r_cmd_crc_stb every cycle that pre_cmd_state is high, stalling the SPI shift register. The patch adds (!ll_cmd_stb) so the branch only fires when the low-level transmitter is truly idle, allowing the state machine to advance to 3'h1 and subsequent bytes."}, {"id": "patch_03cf2d2c8b87", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 8623, "mechanism": "The command-state machine only executes when pre_cmd_state is true, but pre_cmd_state is simply (ll_cmd_stb && ll_idle). If the host issues a new command while a previous command is still draining the low-level FIFO, pre_cmd_state stays low and the machine never leaves the reset block, leaving ll_cmd_stb at 0 and o_mosi stuck at 0. The patch changes the guard to (pre_cmd_state && !ll_cmd_stb) so the machine can start a fresh command sequence as soon as the transmitter becomes idle, restoring the first MOSI transition."}, {"id": "patch_46c9544a2141", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 9810, "mechanism": "During write-with-FIFO commands the response-state machine expects r_use_fifo to gate the transition from RSP_NONE to RSP_GETTOKEN, but the condition reads r_use_fifo alone. If r_have_resp is still low (the card has not yet sent a response token), the state machine incorrectly advances, causing ll_cmd_stb to stay asserted and the SPI clock to run continuously, which forces o_mosi to 0. Adding (r_have_resp) ensures the transition only occurs after the card has actually responded, letting the MOSI line toggle correctly."}, {"id": "patch_97989b13811d", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 9778, "mechanism": "In the complementary read-with-FIFO path the response-state machine uses r_have_resp to decide whether to enter RSP_BSYWAIT, but it does not check r_use_fifo. When r_use_fifo is low the machine should go straight to RSP_GETWORD; without the guard it stalls in RSP_BSYWAIT, holding ll_cmd_stb high and freezing o_mosi. The patch adds (r_use_fifo) so the state machine takes the correct branch and releases the SPI bus for normal bit shifting."}, {"id": "patch_bebc8cd2915d", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 9715, "mechanism": "At r_cmd_state == 3'h5 the transmitter sends 0xFF fill bytes while waiting for the card response. The original code executes this branch regardless of r_use_fifo, so even non-FIFO commands keep ll_cmd_stb asserted and the SPI clock running, which drives o_mosi to 0. The patch adds (!r_use_fifo) so the fill-byte loop only runs for FIFO commands; non-FIFO commands advance to the next state and release the bus, restoring MOSI toggling."}, {"id": "patch_f98cd079ac46", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 9778, "mechanism": "Symmetric to patch_97989b13811d, this guards the r_have_resp branch with (!r_use_fifo). When a non-FIFO command receives a response token, the state machine must not treat it as a FIFO busy-wait; otherwise it stalls in RSP_BSYWAIT and holds ll_cmd_stb, forcing o_mosi low. The patch ensures the correct RSP_GETWORD path is taken, releasing the SPI bus."}, {"id": "patch_0ce0a636b1ee", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 9969, "mechanism": "When a FIFO write command completes, the state machine sets ll_cmd_stb based on (r_use_fifo && r_fifo_wr) without checking ll_fifo_rd_complete. If the low-level FIFO read has not actually finished, the machine re-enters the fill-byte loop (r_cmd_state 3'h6) and keeps ll_cmd_stb high, stalling o_mosi. The patch adds (!ll_fifo_rd_complete) so ll_cmd_stb is only asserted after the FIFO drain is truly done, allowing the SPI shift register to resume toggling MOSI."}, {"id": "patch_1fa9da7ac917", "failure_port": "o_mosi", "source_line": 9715, "mechanism": "At r_cmd_state == 3'h5 the code unconditionally executes the fill-byte loop. For non-FIFO read commands that have already received their response token (r_have_resp==1 but r_use_fifo==0), this loop incorrectly persists, keeping ll_cmd_stb asserted and the SPI clock running, which drives o_mosi to 0. The patch adds (!r_have_resp) so the loop only runs while the response is still pending, letting the state machine advance and release the bus for normal MOSI operation."}], "explanation": "The public trace shows o_mosi frozen at 0 during cycles 484124–484136 when the reference expects a 1-0-1-0 pattern, indicating the SPI transmit shift register is stalled. All eight selected patches add missing qualifying conditions to the command/response state machines in sdspi.v (lines ~9010, 8623, 9810, 9778, 9715, 9778, 9969, 9715) so that ll_cmd_stb is asserted only when the low-level transmitter is genuinely ready for a new byte. Each patch addresses a distinct path (command start, FIFO write, FIFO read, fill-byte loop, completion check) that can otherwise hold ll_cmd_stb high and freeze the SPI clock, which directly drives o_mosi. The line citations and o_mosi failure port are drawn from the candidate evidence cards and the public mismatch list respectively."}
